reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper is that football in-play betting can be modeled using risk-neutral pricing principles borrowed from financial derivatives theory. By treating the sequence of goals as a pair of independent Poisson processes N1_t and N2_t, one constructs artificial underlying assets S1_t and S2_t which are compensated Poisson processes under the risk-neutral measure Q. These processes allow for the derivation of arbitrage-free prices for bets such as match odds, over/under totals, and correct scores. The key mathematical machinery involves Girsanov’s theorem to change measures, ensuring that under Q, the processes become Poisson with risk-neutral intensities λ1 and λ2. Pricing follows from conditional expectations under Q, leading to closed-form expressions for European-style bets. Dynamic hedging is enabled by computing hedge weights that match deltas of the portfolio to those of the underlying score processes. Calibration is performed using least-squares optimization to estimate λ1 and λ2 from observed market mid-prices, weighting each bet according to its liquidity. This framework provides a rigorous foundation for both pricing and replication but assumes constant intensities, which may fail in practice where scoring rates evolve with game state or time.
